headline: Dealing with Smoke Damage: Common Mistakes to Avoid
articleBody: When your home suffers smoke damage, it's a stressful time, and it's easy to make missteps that can actually worsen the situation. One big mistake we often see is trying to clean soot yourself without proper protection or knowledge. Soot particles are tiny and can be harmful if inhaled or spread. Another common pitfall is using standard household cleaners; these can sometimes set the smoke odor or stain surfaces permanently instead of removing them. Don't forget about porous materials like fabrics and upholstery – simply airing them out won't eliminate embedded smoke odor. Many folks also overlook the HVAC system; if it ran during or after the fire, smoke particles are likely circulating throughout your ducts, re-contaminating your home. Lastly, don't delay! The longer smoke and soot sit, the more difficult and costly they become to remove. Avoiding these mistakes and calling in professionals like First To Respond Restoration can save you a lot of headache and ensure your home is truly clean and safe again.
